study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its aim to identify MDD subtypes using subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities relative to normative ranges, and explains the purpose of applying a normative approach (tolerance intervals) to support subtype discovery, reproducibility checks, and evaluation of clinical utility (case–control discriminability). This satisfies both criteria: explicit research objective and rationale for using a normative framework.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "This study aimed to identify MDD subtypes based on subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities using a tolerance interval-based approach. ... We constructed parcel-wise functional connectivity tolerance intervals using healthy controls and identified subject-level extreme functional connectivity profiles in MDD patients. These features were used to identify MDD subtypes... We assessed the reproducibility... Finally, we evaluated whether these subtypes could improve case-control discriminability."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: A NEW normative model is built from healthy controls (HCs). Data source and final HC sample size are provided, with citations to original publications. However, explicit eligibility criteria for HCs and image quality/data completeness standards (and exclusion reasons) are not fully described in this paper; they are deferred to prior publications.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The imaging datasets for MDD used in this study were sourced from the REST-meta-MDD consortium... comprising 1276 MDD patients ... and 1104 HCs... Further demographic, clinical and imaging details are available in previous publications [31, 32]."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Multi-site effects are addressed using ComBat harmonization. However, core covariates (age, sex) are not modeled in the normative tolerance intervals (HC-based). Therefore, site effects are handled, but broader covariate handling within the normative model is limited.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Given the multi-site nature of the data collection... we applied the Combat method to harmonize the functional connections across these sites."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the reference cohort is explicitly identified as the REST-meta-MDD consortium, with URL and citations to the original publications.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The neuroimaging data were sourced from the REST-meta-MDD consortium (http://rfmri.org/REST-meta-MDD) [31, 32]... with 1276 patients with MDD and 1104 healthy controls."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from an existing multi-site dataset were used; per guidance, for SECONDARY data (existing datasets), answer NA for image acquisition protocol.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing follows standard protocols described elsewhere; this paper specifies use of released regional mean time courses (Craddock-200) and explicitly notes that global signal regression was not applied. Software/pipeline names and QC details are not fully reported here.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Preprocessing of the fMRI data followed standard analysis protocols across study sites... For this study, we utilized the released mean time courses for each brain region, as defined in the Craddock 200 brain atlas... Global signal regression was not applied..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For a NEW normative model, internal validation would require testing on samples not used for fitting (e.g., CV/holdout within HCs). The paper constructs HC-based tolerance intervals and then identifies extreme connections; it does not report partitioning/validation of the normative model on held-out HC data. Subsampling and stability analyses pertain to patient feature selection/subtyping, not validation of the HC-derived normative ranges.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We used the 'tolerance' package in R ... to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs... This process was repeated 100 times, with 90% of the MDD patients randomly subsampled in each iteration."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external dataset of healthy individuals is used to validate the normative model. The external analysis applies the pipeline to schizophrenia patients (COBRE), which does not constitute external validation on healthy controls.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "...we examined the specificity of extreme functional connections for MDD by applying the same analysis to schizophrenia patients from the COBRE dataset."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals built on HCs using the R 'tolerance' package; key settings are provided (90% tolerance proportion, 10% confidence).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "First, we used the 'tolerance' package in R ... to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs. Following prior studies, we set a 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative model fit/calibration metrics for the HC-based normative model (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, or coverage). Reported metrics focus on classification performance (SVM) and subtype discriminability rather than normative model performance.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "SVMs trained on extreme functional connections achieved an accuracy of 55.10% for all patients versus HCs... subtype 1 versus HCs 71.66%... subtype 2 versus HCs 63.26%..."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning of the HC reference cohort (e.g., train/validation/test) is reported; per guidance, answer NA when no partitioning is performed.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software/library used for the normative component is specified (R 'tolerance' package). Data availability is clearly stated with a URL. However, versions are not provided and code is only available upon reasonable request, not openly released.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "The data that support the findings of this study are freely available (https://www.scidb.cn/... )."; "The code that generates the findings... available from the corresponding author, upon reasonable request."; "we used the 'tolerance' package in R..."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: SECONDARY data: original publications are cited; diagnostic criteria (DSM-IV) are specified, and final sample size is reported. However, explicit image quality standards and exclusion reasons are not detailed in this paper.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "MDD diagnoses were made by experienced psychiatrists according to DSM-IV criteria... The imaging datasets ... from 25 research sites, comprising 1276 MDD patients..."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses consider clinical covariates beyond demographics: extreme connections are linked to age of onset; medication status is examined via untreated subgroup validation. However, broader covariates (e.g., comorbidities, symptom dimensions beyond HAMD) are limited, and the paper notes restricted clinical data.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "In MDD patients, these extreme functional connections were linked to age of onset..."; "...we validated clustering results in untreated cases..."; "the limited clinical data available prevented us from examining other potential differences between subtypes..."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort data source is specified as REST-meta-MDD with URL and citations.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The imaging datasets for MDD used in this study were sourced from the REST-meta-MDD consortium (http://rfmri.org/REST-meta-MDD) [31, 32]."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: The paper reports clinical cohort sample sizes and summarizes demographics and clinical characteristics (age, sex, HAMD, illness duration, age of onset, medication status, episodicity).
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table 1 reports: sample sizes (MDD n=1276, HCs n=1104), Age, Males %, HAMD, Illness duration, Age of onset, Medication status, Episodicity, Mean FD.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessment measures are specified: DSM-IV for diagnosis and HAMD for symptom severity.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "MDD diagnoses were made ... according to DSM-IV criteria, with symptom severity assessed using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD)."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are operationalized as extreme functional connections falling outside HC-derived tolerance intervals (90% tolerance proportion, 10% confidence). The paper describes directionality in terms of increased vs decreased connectivity patterns across networks and discusses clinical implications (case-control discriminability, links to age of onset and reward-related processes). However, it does not comprehensively define the sign/magnitude interpretation for each deviation nor standardized categorical thresholds beyond the TI settings and consistency criteria.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "...estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals... 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level... Functional connections ... fell outside this range were classified as extreme."; "patients in subtype 1 exhibited increased functional connectivity ... In contrast, patients in subtype 2 demonstrated decreased connectivity..."; "extreme functional connections were linked to age of onset and reward-related processes."
